page: Microsoft Azure D96lds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine hypervised via Microsoft Hyper-V, designed for high-density compute tasks requiring fast local scratch space. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory is configured at 192.0 GB, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor incorporates a 480 MB L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and VAES.

The instance includes 5670 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, while discrete GPU acceleration is not present. Synthetic performance testing shows top-tier multi-threaded processing, reflected in a PassMark CPU score of 108,246.31 and top-decile extended instruction performance. While single-core stress-ng throughput registers in the middle 50% at 2,279.19, parallel throughput is strong at 100,098.18. Memory subsystem benchmarks show small-block cached read bandwidth reaching 7,403.16 GB/sec and uncached 256 MB reads and writes achieving 349.97 GB/sec and 137.53 GB/sec, respectively.

Application and synthetic workload results show top-tier metrics in static web serving at 150.35 GB/sec, Redis SET operations at 159.81 million operations per second, and PassMark database operations. With integrated AMX support, LLM prompt processing speeds achieve top-tier rates across small, medium, and large model architectures. Because memory allocation is constrained to 2.0 GB per vCPU, this instance trades per-thread memory capacity for high core density and local NVMe throughput, making it suitable for distributed compile jobs, batch ETL, web serving layers, and high-concurrency database workloads utilizing fast local scratch disks.
description: Microsoft Azure D96lds_v7 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The instance delivers 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores, paired with 192.0 GB of memory and 5670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs. Architectural features include a large 480 MB L3 cache, AVX-512, and Intel AMX hardware acceleration. Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier multi-core PassMark computational results, alongside high-throughput operational scores exceeding 159 million Redis SET operations per second and 150 GB/sec in static web serving. While the 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation represents a lower memory-to-core ratio, the high parallel execution capacity and local NVMe capacity provide an efficient resource balance for multi-threaded processing, database operations, web tiers, and batch compression workloads.
